manifest.description: Investigate an installed native utility and reconstruct its unbounded path-processing behavior using real model inference, independent executable checks and automated project governance.

blocks.title: Investigate GNU basename and plan reconstruction
blocks.instructions: Investigate GNU basename through run_tool target. Read --help and probe empty paths, trailing slashes, /, suffix removal, -a, -s, -z and combined options. Return artifact {spec:string,instructions:string}: a concise observed specification and detailed instructions for another agent to write a general algorithmic CLI clone. Do not write implementation code. Cite probes in spec. Limit to five tool calls and then finish.

payload.summary: The implementation matched `/usr/bin/basename` on stdout and exit status in 41 local comparisons, including generated paths and suffixes, option clusters, empty operands, and usage errors (shell evidence `7ab86f`). One requirement is impossible through the mandated interface. Node 26.13.0 exposed the distinct input byte sequences `ff`, `fe`, and `ef bf bd` as the same `process.argv` string (shell evidence `4f398c`). The clone therefore preserves valid UTF-8 arguments but cannot guarantee parity for invalid UTF-8. Exact help, version, diagnostics, and output-write failure behavior were not verified. No files were modified.

block.instructions:
Write a general algorithmic CLI clone; do not use a finite lookup table or consult filesystem paths. Preserve argument bytes end to end rather than requiring valid Unicode. Parse options left to right only until the first non-option operand or '--'. Support clustered -a and -z; -s consumes the rest of its cluster, otherwise the next argument, even when that argument starts with '-'. Support the documented long options, --suffix=value, separate suffix arguments, and unambiguous long-option abbreviations. Repeated suffix options replace the prior suffix; any -s enables multiple mode. Reject unknown options, missing required arguments, and values supplied to argument-free options. Handle help/version during option parsing using the reference's conventional success behavior; exact version output was not probed. After parsing, require at least one operand. In default mode permit one NAME and an optional positional SUFFIX; reject a third operand before emitting output. In multiple mode treat every operand as NAME, with the last -s suffix applied uniformly, if present. For each NAME: preserve empty input as empty; remove trailing slash bytes; if a nonempty input consists only of slashes, return a single slash; otherwise take the bytes after the last remaining slash. Do not normalize '.', '..', backslashes or embedded control bytes. If the suffix is nonempty, strictly shorter than this component and matches its terminal bytes, remove exactly one occurrence. Emit each result followed by LF, or NUL when -z was parsed, including empty results. Return 0 on success and 1 for observed usage errors; keep errors on stderr and stdout empty for argument validation failures. Match the reference's diagnostic structure where practical: missing operand, extra operand identifying the third positional operand, option-specific errors, then a help hint. Exact quoting and program-name prefixes can depend on invocation and locale; observed usage errors used 'basename:' while option errors used '/usr/bin/basename:'. Validate independently against the cited probes, then use generated byte-string paths and suffixes of varied lengths, repeated slashes, empty arguments, suffix equality, option clusters, repeated suffixes, '--', and option-looking operands. Keep processing unbounded by fixed path-length tables. Remaining unverified details include exact help/version parity, locale-dependent diagnostics and output-write failures; do not claim these were experimentally established.
Produce artifact.files["main.ts"] as a complete portable Node.js TypeScript CLI implementation compatible with Node 26 native type stripping, with no Bun-specific APIs, with no external commands or dependencies. Parse process.argv.slice(2), write stdout and exit status. The reference command is available through run_tool target. Handle -a/--multiple, -s/--suffix including --suffix=..., -z/--zero, combined short options, -- separator, single-operand optional suffix, errors. No lookup tables; handle arbitrary path strings algorithmically. Match stdout and exit status; stderr text, --help, --version and filesystem input are outside this contract. Previous verification reports contain feedback for retries.
